**The web UI has this same bug, and the in-flight fix #26432 is TUI-only — it won't cover the web client.**

Confirmed on opencode **1.16.2** (`opencode serve`, accessed from a browser/phone). The web client fetches `GET /session` **without `roots=true`** and filters children client-side (`sessions.filter(s => !s.parentID)`). So the server's default `limit=100` is spent on a mix of root + subagent sessions, and roots get evicted under heavy subagent use — the same root cause described here.

Measured on a store with **241 root + ~1032 child** sessions:

```
GET /session                    -> 100 total =  36 roots + 64 children
GET /session?roots=true         -> 100 total = 100 roots
GET /session?roots=true&limit=N -> all 241 roots
```

Only **36 of 241** roots reach the web UI, and during multi-agent bursts (last 24h here: 59 child updates vs 6 root, ~10:1) even freshly-created root sessions drop out of the window within hours and never reappear (`time_updated` now below the 100th-newest). Data is intact on disk throughout.

Since #26432 only touches the TUI dialog, please also have the **web** session list pass `roots=true` (the API already supports it). Happy to test a build.

One thing I would check here is whether the failing models are being routed through the same tool-call contract as the models that work. Qwen2.5-Coder can be good at code, but that does not mean it has the same native tool-call behavior or chat-template assumptions as gpt-oss / Qwen3.

The symptom "outputs the tool call but does not actually do it" often means the model is producing a textual imitation of the call instead of a structured call the runtime recognizes. I would separate three cases in the logs:

1. raw model output contains JSON-like/tool-call text
2. parser converts it into an internal tool invocation
3. executor actually receives the invocation

If 1 happens but 2 does not, this is probably a template/parser compatibility issue rather than a coding-quality issue. If 2 happens but 3 does not, it is more likely an OpenCode execution-path issue.

For local coding models, I have found it useful to make the boundary explicit: model generates open-ended code, but the runtime owns exact tool routing and validation. Otherwise a small model can look like it "knows" the tool call while only emitting text that resembles one.

Hi everyone — I came across this issue while searching for exactly this feature, and I just wanted to say that I'd find it really valuable too.

Being able to correct or refine a message — both the user's and the model's — without losing the entire conversation context (and all the compute that went into it) is something I consider fundamental for a smooth workflow. Small typos, misunderstood intents, or half-correct code blocks happen often, and the current all-or-nothing undo makes it harder to keep a clean, maintainable session.

At the end of the day, LLMs are really just fancy autocomplete — we iterate with them, back and forth, and the ability to edit any part of the conversation feels like a natural part of that flow. Some commercial closed-source products already have this, and I would be really happy to see it on this great open-source solution. It makes a real difference in daily advanced usage.

I've actually started working on a local implementation — a simple inline edit button on messages that opens a textarea, lets you modify the content, and saves it back via the SDK's part.update API. It's still rough, but the core flow works.

I'd love to contribute this upstream if there's interest. Could someone point me in the right direction? Should I open a draft PR for early feedback, or is there a discussion thread or design doc I should follow first?

Thanks!

This issue is about a behavioral inconsistency in v1.16.2:

- The v1.16.2 release notes present backgrounding running subagents as a normal improvement:
  "Running subagents can now be sent to the background so you can keep working."
- The TUI shows the keybind hint by default, e.g. "ctrl+b background" or a custom "f8 background".
- But the endpoint still returns false unless OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true is set.
- There is no toast/error, so the shortcut appears broken.

Repro:
1. Start opencode v1.16.2 without OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS.
2. Start a foreground subagent.
3. Observe the TUI hint: "ctrl+b background" (or custom keybind).
4. Press the keybind. Nothing happens.
5. POST /experimental/session/{sessionID}/background returns false.
6. GET /experimental/tool/ids does not include task_status.
7. Restart with OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true and the feature becomes available.

Expected:
Either:
- remove the env gate for this feature in v1.16.2, or
- hide the TUI keybind hint unless the flag is enabled, and show an explicit error/toast instead of silently returning false.

This is related to the flag, but it is not just a docs-table issue.

## Additional details for GLM 5.1 / z.ai

I'm experiencing the same **"terminated" / "Network error"** issue specifically with the **z.ai (GLM 5.1)** provider.

**Exact error:**
```
Network error, error id: 2026060622490410eb8ceede9541e9, please try again later
```

**Context:**
- Provider: z.ai (GLM 5.1) via OpenCode Go
- OpenCode version: 1.16.2
- OS: macOS
- Error occurs during provider requests, session terminates without retry

**Root cause analysis (from source code):**
In `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts` in the `fromError()` function, only `ECONNRESET` is classified as retryable (`isRetryable: true`). Other transient network errors like:
- `ETIMEDOUT`, `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN` (DNS)
- `ECONNREFUSED`, `EHOSTUNREACH`, `ENETUNREACH`, `EPIPE`
- Text patterns: `fetch failed`, `socket hang up`, `terminated`, `other side closed`

...fall through to the generic `UnknownError` case which **is not retried** by the retry logic in `retry.ts`.

**Local fix tested:**
I widened the classification in `fromError()` to include all transient system error codes and text patterns above, classifying them as `APIError(isRetryable: true)`. This allows the existing retry mechanism to handle them correctly.

PR #30638 addresses exactly this issue.

Hope this helps prioritize the fix for the z.ai/GLM provider which appears particularly susceptible to these transient network errors.

Just to clarify per the bot — this is specifically about the **hosted**  endpoints, not a self-hosted server.

**Affected:**
-  (Zen/free)
-  (Go/paid)

**What I found:**

The API backend is alive — only the OPTIONS preflight is broken:

| Endpoint | Method | Result |
|---|---|---|
|  | POST | 401 "Invalid API key" (API works) |
|  | POST | 401 "Invalid API key" (API works) |
|  | GET | 200 (full model list returned) |
|  | OPTIONS (preflight) | ❌ 404 — HTML "Not Found" page, no CORS headers |
|  | OPTIONS (preflight) | ❌ 404 — same thing |

**Root cause I traced:**
The gateway doesn't route OPTIONS requests to the API handler — they fall through to the frontend SPA router, which returns a 404 HTML page. Needs to respond with:
- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`
- `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, GET, OPTIONS`
- `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type`
- `Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400`

Same class of bug as #10047 (basic auth blocking OPTIONS), just at a different layer.

I built a workaround for myself (GM_xmlhttpRequest bridge to bypass CORS entirely) but obviously a real fix would be better.

- Tool surface includes Anthropic's "deferred tools" pattern — tools like `RemoteTrigger`, `WebFetch`, `TaskCreate`, and all `mcp__claude_ai_*__*` connectors are not in the default tool list; the model loads schemas on demand via a `ToolSearch select:<name>` call.

**Symptom**
- After a context summarization / compaction, previously-loaded deferred tool schemas drop out of the model's working tool set.
- On the next turn the model attempts the call directly (it "remembers" the tool worked earlier), and opencode prints:

  ```
  invalid [tool=RemoteTrigger, error=Model tried to call unavailable tool 'RemoteTrigger'. <full available-tools list dumped here>
  ```

- The model then recovers (re-fetches the schema, retries), and the user-facing call eventually succeeds. So the error is purely cosmetic — but it's loud and includes the entire available-tools list, which dwarfs the actual response.

**Why this matters even when not using open-source models**

This is the documented Anthropic pattern for keeping the tool schema cheap. Deferred-tool drops after compaction are *expected*; the harness recovery is by design. opencode rendering each one as a top-level error is the part that's wrong.

**Asks (echoing the original report and adding one)**
1. Filter the `invalid` internal tool out of user-facing output (per the original report).
2. Treat "tool not in current schema but recoverable on next turn" as a debug-level event, not an error-level one — `logLevel: WARN` should hide it.
3. (Optional) Truncate the available-tools list dump in any user-visible rendering — listing 100+ tools in a terminal error is the biggest contributor to the perceived spam.

Happy to provide a sanitized session transcript if helpful.

Adding a concrete use case to support this request: **code intelligence provider status in the right panel**.

### The problem

When a developer uses an MCP-based static analysis tool like [gograph](https://github.com/ozgurcd/gograph), opencode has no visibility into whether the tool's index is fresh. The agent silently queries a stale graph and produces wrong results — and the developer has no way to know without leaving opencode.

LSP servers already solve this for language servers: their status appears in the right panel. The same treatment is missing for tools that build local indexes outside of LSP.

### Concrete use case

gograph is a Go AST analysis tool that already ships as a working MCP server (`gograph mcp`). When configured in `opencode.json`, all its tools are available to the LLM. The missing piece is a freshness indicator visible in the TUI:

```
Code Intelligence
  gograph   ready   75 files · 622 symbols · built 4m ago
```

If the graph is stale:

```
  gograph   STALE   3 source files changed since last build
```

### Proposed minimal contract

A provider exposes a small JSON payload (via stdout, a local socket, or a named pipe — whatever fits the plugin model):

```json
{
  "name": "gograph",
  "kind": "code-intelligence",
  "status": "ready | stale | building | error",
  "details": {
    "indexed_files": 75,
    "symbols": 622,
    "last_built": "2026-06-06T15:00:00Z",
    "stale_files": 0
  }
}
```

The panel row is driven entirely by this payload — no opencode-side special-casing per tool.

### Why this strengthens the existing status bar widget request

A generic "register a status bar widget" API is powerful but abstract. A code intelligence provider interface gives it a concrete, motivating use case with an immediate reference implementation ready to ship. The gograph side of this is a single `gograph status --serve` subcommand — minimal surface area.

Happy to collaborate on the design if there is appetite for this direction.

AI assisted analysis points to some fun CJS vs module bundling issues. I personally doubt this is an upstream bun issue, but it does look like it's something to do with the bundling

# Claude analysis

Found it. @aws-sdk/token-providers CJS uses await import('@aws-sdk/nested-clients/sso-oidc') — a dynamic ESM import(). That loads the dist-es version of nested-clients/sso-oidc, which in turn does import { ... } from "@smithy/core/config" as ESM. Bun caches that module as an ESM namespace object. Then when credential-provider-ini CJS does var config = require('@smithy/core/config'), Bun hands back the already-cached ESM namespace — where named exports are Symbol-keyed, not string-keyed.
This is a Bun bug: mixing require() and dynamic import() of the same module within the same runtime causes the module cache to return an ESM namespace object to a CJS require() call, breaking property access.
The workaround is to ensure @aws-sdk/credential-providers and its whole dep tree load consistently as ESM. The cleanest way: use the dist-es entry directly for the packages that have the mismatch, by adding overrides in package.json to point @aws-sdk/token-providers and @aws-sdk/credential-provider-ini at their ESM builds — or, more practically, file this as a Bun bug and in the meantime avoid fromNodeProviderChain in favour of building the credential chain manually using only ESM-safe providers.
